authority: experiment-owner direction to continue without per-run approval
trigger: The Claude Code Beets control r6 failed at stage setup-deps with exit 2. The uv installer reported: failed to copy ... No space left on device (os error 28).

state_found.note: A single lane rsyncs a full repository checkout and builds a fixture virtualenv, so a lane needs roughly a gigabyte to start.

action_taken.freed: 12.06 GB by deleting lane roots not referenced by any receipt; 50 referenced roots retained

prior_diagnoses_now_in_doubt.what_was_claimed: The OpenCode lane failures of 2026-10-02 and 10-03 -- TokenJuice on Fastify stalling at step 14 and Serena on Beets at step 2, both with zero errors and zero quota entries -- were attributed to provider throughput being too low to finish a task.
prior_diagnoses_now_in_doubt.why_that_is_now_uncertain: Those lanes ran while the disk was at or near exhaustion. A lane that cannot write is indistinguishable from a lane that is waiting on a slow provider, from the controller's side: both produce a task that runs out its budget leaving a zero-byte event file and no error.
prior_diagnoses_now_in_doubt.what_the_host_check_actually_showed: The host measurements that ruled out local causes were taken on 2026-09-26, when 4.0G remained free. They were never repeated during the October failures. Asserting the host was healthy during those runs was an inference from a stale measurement, not an observation.
prior_diagnoses_now_in_doubt.status: Not retracted and not confirmed. The October failures have two candidate causes and the evidence retained cannot separate them. The degradation receipts stand as records of the failures; their attribution to provider throughput is downgraded to unresolved.

what_would_separate_them: Relaunch now that 13G is free. If lanes complete, disk exhaustion was the cause and the provider-slowness reading was wrong. If they fail identically with ample disk, provider throughput is confirmed.

spend.note: The r6 lane failed at dependency setup before any provider turn. Zero spend.

preventable: This was foreseeable. Lane roots accumulate about a gigabyte per run and nothing prunes them; I deleted 4.6G on 2026-09-26 and did not check again across sixteen further lanes. A disk check belongs in the pre-launch sequence alongside the credential and pin checks.

attribution_resolved_20261004.question: Whether the October OpenCode failures were caused by disk exhaustion or by provider throughput. Both produce a task that exhausts its budget leaving a zero-byte event file and no error.
attribution_resolved_20261004.test: Relaunch both a Claude Code lane and an OpenCode lane with 12-13G free.
attribution_resolved_20261004.result_claude_code: baseline-claude-code-no-mcp beets r6 completed 6/6 at 309,469.7 after failing the day before at setup-deps with no space left on device. Disk was that failure's cause.
attribution_resolved_20261004.result_opencode: retrieval-serena-opencode-mcp-v1 beets r3 failed again with 12G free, reaching task-01 step 11, zero errors, zero quota, zero-byte event file. Disk was not its cause.
attribution_resolved_20261004.conclusion: The two failure families are distinct and were correctly separated only after the disk was cleared. The Claude Code setup-deps failure was disk. The OpenCode lane timeouts of 10-02 and 10-03 are confirmed as provider-side: they reproduce with ample disk, on both fixtures, with no error surfaced.
attribution_resolved_20261004.status_of_the_earlier_downgrade: The provider-throughput attribution recorded on 10-03 for the OpenCode failures is restored. The caution that prompted the downgrade was still correct methodology -- the host evidence I had cited was stale -- but the conclusion it questioned has now been tested directly and holds.
attribution_resolved_20261004.opencode_failure_count: Three consecutive OpenCode lanes have now failed in this shape: tokenjuice fastify r3 at step 14, serena beets r3 at step 2 and again at step 11. The OpenAI halt stands.
attribution_resolved_20261004.claude_code_unaffected: Claude Code lanes have completed throughout, including this one, on a separate Anthropic credential.
